intent: Check the board/history after PSI-102 (merged) and root-cause the pre-existing /auth/sign-in bug it filed as a follow-up instead of leaving it unowned.
summary: Verified PSI-102 landed on master (PR #49, merged; the earlier PR #48 was closed with a conflict). Investigated the /auth/sign-in 500 PSI-102's history entry attributed to a `submit-button.tsx` formContext bug. Confirmed via @tanstack/react-form's own source (createFormHook.js) that `formComponents` registered through `createFormHook` (SubmitButton here) are plain components assigned onto the `form` object; `formContext.Provider` is established only inside `<form.AppForm>`, which none of the app's forms used. Reproduced live: before the fix, curling a running dev server's /auth/sign-in returned HTTP 200 but the HTML body carried the `formContext` throw and never rendered the real form (PSI-102 saw a 500 because sign-in also lacked a Suspense boundary around its `useSearchParams()`, matching the exact pattern dashboard/kanban/page.tsx already has to guard against). Fixed both: added `<React.Suspense>` around sign-in's form component, and wrapped the `<form>` in `<form.AppForm>` in all 5 places that call `form.SubmitButton` (sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, reset-password, invite-user-dialog) -- found by grepping every `SubmitButton` caller, not just the one PSI-102 hit. Re-tested against a live dev server: /auth/sign-in now renders the real form ('Enter your email and password' present, no formContext text). tsc clean, oxlint 0/0, bun test 28/28, next build clean. This unblocks manual browser acceptance for every future card in the calendar -> kanban -> finance pipeline, since all of them sit behind sign-in.

changes.note: Suspense boundary for useSearchParams + form.AppForm wrap

decisions.decision: Fix all 5 `form.SubmitButton` call sites, not just /auth/sign-in
decisions.reason: Root-cause fix: grepping SubmitButton's callers showed the same missing-wrapper bug everywhere, not a sign-in-specific issue; patching only the page PSI-102 happened to test would have left 4 more broken forms
alternatives: Fix only /auth/sign-in since that's what was reported

verification.manual: bun test: 28/28 pass. Ran `bun run dev` locally and curled /auth/sign-in before and after the fix: before, HTTP 200 with the formContext throw embedded in the HTML and no form content; after, the real form renders ('Enter your email and password' present, no formContext text).
